summary: Priority-queue backlog on high-token requests causing client timeouts and 504s
description:
Issue summary:

Customers on Dedicated capacity are seeing requests with very large prompt + max_tokens budgets either get long tail latencies or terminate with client-observed timeouts (HTTP 504 or streaming cutoffs). Problem appears when requests request >180k total token budget (prompt + max_tokens) and coincide with sustained traffic causing backlog in the serving priority queue.

Impact:
- Multiple customers report streaming cuts or finalization failures after ~60-120s.
- HarborAnalytics reports several failed batch jobs and a customer-facing data export pipeline timed out twice.
- Error phenotype: final chunks never arrive or are missing, client sees 504 or connection closed by server after HTTP keepalive.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated pool: pool-dedicated-east-3
- Regions impacted: us-east
- Models: redwood/open-7b-v2 and gptq-13b-ctx-ext pinned by customers

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1. Send a chat.generate request with a 150k token prompt and max_tokens 40k to a pinned model on Dedicated pool-dedicated-east-3.
2. Under synthetic load (peak concurrency ~80%), observe that request enters the runtime and experiences long queuing delays, then streaming output stalls during finalization.
3. Client observes 504 or streaming connection closure after ~90s, despite backend logs showing the request not fully finalized.

Logs / Evidence snippets:
- Serving logs show request queued for 45s before kernel selection.
- Scheduler trace: backpressure triggers and lower-priority finalization tasks are preempted by large batched generations.
- Kernel telemetry: fallback to a slower attention kernel after a memory allocation failure on one host (retry path increased token processing time by 2.7x).
- HarborAnalytics customer logs attached in ticket thread (redacted).
comments: 2026-03-10 09:18 - Support (Aisha): Initial triage with customer. Asked for request examples, tokens, and model pinning. Customer provided sanitized request IDs and related logs.

2026-03-10 10:05 - SRE (Marcus): Reproduced locally against pool-dedicated-east-3 with load generator. Observed queue depth spikes and long-tail latencies when several 100k+ token requests are in flight.

2026-03-10 13:42 - Engineering (Elena R.): Noted a regression introduced by scheduler weight tuning PR last week (PR 4819) that increased batching preference for large-sequence workloads; adding here for triage.

2026-03-11 08:30 - Support (Aisha): Sent temporary mitigations to HarborAnalytics: set max_tokens to 20k and split prompts into chunked calls while we investigate. Customer reports immediate reduction in failures.

2026-03-12 11:22 - Engineering (Marcus): Applied temporary hotfix to scheduler in staging to deprioritize long-tail finalization tasks; running soak tests now. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4821
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Scheduler weighting change increased preference for packing large requests into continuous batches which starve finalization steps, causing streaming final chunks to be delayed until the request times out.
Hypothesis 2: KV-cache eviction thrashing on very long-context requests forces kernel fallback and extra memory copies, increasing per-token latency for a subset of hosts.

Hypothesis 3: When large requests coincide with high concurrency, the priority queue misreports 'in-progress' state and doesn't account for finalize-phase CPU-bound work, leaving sockets open until client timeout.
Telemetry findings: Hosts hitting OOM/retry clearly correlated with slower kernel fallback. Queue metrics show P50 queue delay 1.2s but P99 queue delay 58s during incidents.
Customer correlation: HarborAnalytics incidents lined up with our scheduled maintenance window where one host had transient disk IO contention.
resolution: Workaround provided to customer: reduce max_tokens to <=20k or chunk prompts; use dedicated pinned smaller-ctx model variant where possible. Technical fixes: rolled back scheduler weight change (PR 4819) and deployed hotfix to deprioritize finalization tasks in the priority queue (PR 4821). Also applied kernel-selection guard to avoid fallback path on hosts with recent memory retrials. Post-deploy metrics show P99 latency for large requests reduced from ~95s to ~28s and streaming cutoffs stopped for the test cohort. Follow-ups: full postmortem and a permanent scheduler tuning with guardrails for long-token requests, update runbook with explicit mitigation steps, offer HarborAnalytics 2 weeks of expedited support credit.
